property_summary: Any caller who is not the current owner must never be able to change the owner via transferOwnership; the bug's removal of the onlyOwner modifier allows a non-owner caller to set a new owner.
For any address newOwner, after a non-owner calls transferOwnership and fails, the owner must remain unchanged; the buggy version incorrectly updates owner to msg.sender.

For any caller, after a successful transferOwnership, the new owner must equal the passed _newOwner parameter; the buggy version instead sets the owner to the caller (msg.sender), violating this rule when caller and _newOwner differ.

For any admissible actors (currentOwner, newOwner) where newOwner != currentOwner, when a non-owner calls transferOwnership the call must revert and the owner must remain unchanged; the buggy version incorrectly updates owner to msg.sender.

After a successful onlyOwner call to transferOwnership, the owner must equal the passed _newOwner parameter; the buggy version sets owner to msg.sender instead, violating equality when the caller and _newOwner differ.

For any caller who is the current owner, after transferOwnership(_newOwner) completes successfully, the new owner must equal _newOwner; the buggy version sets owner to msg.sender, violating equality when the caller differs from _newOwner.
The reference contract allows transferOwnership only when called by the current owner, while the buggy version allows any caller to change the owner.
For any non-owner, transferOwnership must always revert due to the onlyOwner modifier, but the mutant breaks this by allowing the call to succeed without changing the owner.

For any caller, after transferOwnership the stored owner must equal the input address if the caller is the current owner, otherwise it must remain unchanged; the mutant violates this by never updating owner even when called by the owner.
After a successful transferOwnership, the public getter 'owner' must return the new owner argument; the buggy version leaves it unchanged.

For any two distinct non-zero addresses acting as caller and new owner, a successful call to transferOwnership must change the public owner to the new owner argument; the bug breaks this because it deletes the assignment, leaving owner unchanged.
